title: VPS 3 Salary: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Our Guide
description: Learn how to convert a VPS 3 salary hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes tax, super, and comparisons with the National Minimum Wage.
salarySummary: For a VPS 3 employee working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I convert my VPS 3 hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week and then by 52 weeks. For example, $35/hour × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime or allowances.

faqs.q: Is the VPS 3 salary above the National Minimum Wage?
faqs.a: Yes, VPS 3 rates are set by enterprise agreement and are typically well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). Always check your specific agreement.

faqs.q: Does the VPS 3 salary include casual loading?
faqs.a: No, VPS 3 roles are usually permanent. Casual loading of 25% applies only to casual employees under awards. If you are a casual VPS employee, your rate may include loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your VPS 3 Salary

If you're looking at a VPS 3 salary, you likely have an hourly rate or an annual offer. Converting between the two is straightforward, but you need to account for the standard 38-hour week, tax, and superannuation. This guide explains how to use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool and what the numbers mean.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee, the standard is 38 hours per week. So if your VPS 3 hourly rate is $35, your annual gross is $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. This is the figure before tax and super.

You can also calculate fortnightly pay: weekly pay × 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × 38. For $35/hour, weekly = $1,330, fortnightly = $2,660. This is useful for budgeting or comparing with salary offers that quote fortnightly amounts.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for award-free employees. However, most employees, including VPS staff, are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates.

The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award (SCHADS) has specific rates that increased from 1 December 2026. VPS 3 salary is typically governed by the Victorian Public Service Enterprise Agreement, which is not a federal award but still uses the same conversion principles. The minimum rates in that agreement are generally above the National Minimum Wage.

### Casual Loading and Your VPS 3 Salary

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate usually includes a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). For VPS casual roles, check your agreement. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it. Never enter a rate that already includes loading into our timesheet; use the base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox. The tool will then add 25% automatically.

### Tax and Superannuation

Your take-home pay depends on tax brackets. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator to see what you keep after tax.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. So if your VPS 3 salary is $69,160, your employer contributes an additional $8,299.20 in super (12% of $69,160). This is not included in your gross pay but is an extra benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Example: Converting a VPS 3 Hourly Rate

Let's say your VPS 3 hourly rate is $38.50. Annual gross = $38.50 × 38 × 52 = $76,076. Fortnightly gross = $2,926. After tax (using 2026–27 rates and Medicare), your annual take-home would be approximately $59,000 (estimate). Super at 12% adds $9,129.12 per year.

Compare this to the National Minimum Wage: $26.44/hour gives $52,217.44 annual gross. The VPS 3 rate is significantly higher, reflecting the skilled nature of the role. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which is about $108,352 annually. VPS 3 salaries are typically below that average but still provide a solid base.

### Important Considerations

This conversion assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For accurate VPS 3 salary rates, refer to your enterprise agreement or the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) if applicable. You can also use our [reference tables](/data) for common rates across awards.

### Using Our Tools

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate. If you are casual, tick the box to add 25% loading. The tool calculates weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual figures, plus estimated tax and super. It's designed for award-covered employees and those on the National Minimum Wage. For VPS 3 salary, you can enter your agreed hourly rate and see the full breakdown.

### Summary

Converting a VPS 3 salary from hourly to annual is simple: multiply by 38 and 52. Remember that the National Minimum Wage is a floor, and award or agreement rates are higher. Always check your specific pay guide. Use our tools to estimate take-home pay and super. Whether you are negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, understanding the conversion helps you make informed decisions.
